headline: The models still bring only light rain tonight into early Wednesday (wettest 3 hours 0.06 to 0.12 in), so the rating card stays at none; the near-record late-morning king tides and gusty winds remain the bigger story.

summary.text: Small nudge up, still light: HRRR 0.03 to 0.12 in and RRFS 0.02 to 0.07 in for the wettest 3 hours; NBM eased to 0.06 in. Consensus 0.035 to 0.07 in.
Wettest 3 hours: ECMWF 0.12 in, HRRR 0.12 (GFS copies it), RRFS 0.07, NBM 0.06. Storm totals 0.06 to 0.23 in. Good agreement on a quick, light frontal rain.
Rating card consensus 0.07 in: no street flooding expected. Yellow (garage) needs about 0.71 in in 3 hours or a 0.40 in hour; the wettest model hour is 0.09 in.
Dry today. Light rain from this evening, heaviest roughly midnight to 5 AM Wednesday as the front passes, done by late morning. Thanksgiving and Friday dry; rain returns Sunday.
The heaviest rain overlaps the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM, running about 8.5 ft with surge, so the channel drains slowly until about 4 AM. Channel low: 0.13 ft at 7 AM.
Before this evening: clear street drain grates and yard drains. Tonight: gusts near 40 mph can cut power to the pumps. Stay off the Bay shore at late-morning high tides.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Dry today with high clouds thickening and southeast winds increasing ahead of a cold front. NWS San Francisco (discussion issued 3:43 AM, short term updated 1:27 AM) has the front moving through faster than earlier thought, crossing the Bay Area after midnight and the Central Coast before 6 AM, with most rain done by late morning Wednesday. They call it a slightly improved forecast for impacts. Most places see gusts to about 40 mph with the front, 50 mph or more in gaps and passes. Thunderstorm chances are down to about 10 to 15 percent for the North Bay and Bay Area; a thunderstorm would raise rain rates locally, otherwise the rain should be steady and manageable. This NWS discussion gives no Peninsula rain total (yesterday's issue had 0.5 to 1 in). Thanksgiving and Friday dry and mild; more rain likely Sunday, with a stronger system the middle of next week. The Coastal Flood Warning for the San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines runs until 4 PM Thursday.

sections.title: What changed and model trends
sections.text:
Since last evening's discussion the models have moved slightly closer together around a light, quick frontal rain. HRRR and RRFS came up a little, NBM came down, and nothing approaches a burst.

Wettest 3 hours / storm total, 7 AM Tuesday to 7 AM Friday:
• HRRR (5 AM Tue run, out to 4 AM Thu): 0.12 / 0.12 in, all of it about 3 to 5 AM Wednesday, with a peak hour of 0.09 in (4 to 5 AM). Up from 0.03 / 0.04 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends midnight Wednesday night): 0.008 in per 15 minutes 3 to 4 AM, then 0.024 in per 15 minutes 4 to 5 AM Wednesday, then dry.
• RRFS (10 PM Mon run): 0.07 / 0.07 in, about midnight to 2 AM Wednesday. Up from 0.02 / 0.02 in.
• NBM: 0.06 / 0.06 in, about midnight to 3 AM Wednesday. Down from 0.13 / 0.21 in.
• ECMWF: 0.12 / 0.23 in, the wettest and longest: about 0.01 in per hour from 7 PM tonight, then 0.03 to 0.04 in per hour 10 PM to 4 AM. Up slightly from 0.08 / 0.17 in.
• GFS: again identical to HRRR hour for hour, so no independent information.

Consensus (HRRR 0.12 × 1.25 = 0.14, RRFS 0.07, NBM 0.06): middle value 0.07 in, up from 0.035 in, so the rating card stays at none. HRRR has under-forecast big local bursts here by about 3×, but even three times its 3-hour amount (about 0.35 in) stays well below the 0.71 in Yellow threshold, and its wettest hour would have to more than quadruple to reach the 0.40 in one-hour trigger.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (now running to 1 AM Thursday) is about 1.3 to 1.4 ft above the predicted high tides at Redwood City and about 1.0 to 1.7 ft above the lows. This morning's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:02 AM runs about 10.9 ft. This evening's -1.5 ft low at 6:28 PM runs about -0.4 to 0.2 ft, an easy time for the channel to drain before the rain.

The heaviest rain overlaps the 7.1 ft high at 1:12 AM Wednesday: the model has 7.2 ft at midnight, 8.3 ft at 1 AM, 8.5 ft at 2 AM, 7.7 ft at 3 AM, 6.4 ft at 4 AM and 5.2 ft at 5 AM. RRFS and NBM put their rain right on top of that high, so the channel drains slowly then; HRRR's rain comes 3 to 5 AM on a falling tide. At rates under 0.1 in per hour this should not matter on the street. Wednesday's 9.5 ft king tide at 11:46 AM runs about 10.9 ft, after the rain has ended.

NWS: at the San Francisco gauge, highs 2.4 ft above normal this morning, 2.7 ft Wednesday, 2.2 ft Thursday and 2.0 ft Friday and Saturday, including up to 1.6 ft of surge, approaching the highest tide ever recorded there.

Channel: at Alameda de las Pulgas 0.13 ft at 7 AM, flat between 0.12 and 0.15 ft for 24 hours (Flood Monitoring 3.18 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at 5:13 AM, its latest report (Flood Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry on the street. The Caltrain rain gauge recorded no rain in the 24 hours to 5:13 AM. NWS reports patchy fog and low clouds early with high clouds streaming in from the west; clouds lower and winds pick up as the front approaches this evening.

sections.title: Uncertainty
sections.text: Low for today: dry. For tonight into Wednesday morning the models agree on light rain, all wettest 3-hour amounts between 0.06 and 0.12 in, which keeps street-flooding risk low. The remaining wildcard is a thunderstorm along the front (NWS 10 to 15 percent), which could briefly exceed every model. Timing differs by a few hours: RRFS and NBM center the rain on the 1:12 AM high tide, HRRR a few hours later. The more certain hazards are tidal flooding along the Bay shore at the late-morning high tides through Thursday and gusts tonight.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Today before evening: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains; secure loose items ahead of the wind.
• Tonight through early Wednesday: gusts near 40 mph; outages can slow the pumps.
• No need to move cars on current guidance; if a heavy downpour or thunderstorm does develop overnight, move them out of the cul-de-sac and take timestamped photos.
• NWS advice for holiday travel: wait until Wednesday afternoon if you can.
• Stay away from the Bay shore, tidal sloughs and low shoreline roads at the late-morning high tides through Thursday; don't walk or drive through moving water.
